profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: This is a full-contact relationship between the driver, the wedges, and basic arithmetic. The ball gets in play just often enough to keep hope alive, then the rest of the bag shows up with crowbars. The short game has had a couple decent moments, but the bigger story is the parade of doubles, three-putts, and soul-crushing approach days that turn fine-looking holes into garbage fires. This file screams volatile: one segment looks survivable, the next looks like the card got run over by a mower.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.profile: When the irons show up, this dude can absolutely mug a course. The problem is the rest of the bag keeps acting like it’s in witness protection. There’s enough pop with the long sticks to keep the ceiling interesting, and the ball-striking through the middle is the part that keeps the whole operation from collapsing. But the putter has been a petty little thief, and the tee game has leaked just enough to make every good stretch feel like it needs an apology. Real golf, but with a few loose screws.

profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.tagline: TEE SHOT DRAMA, SHORT-GAME SIDE QUEST
profiles.profile: This file is a weird little blender: the driver has been a liability, the irons have flashed, and somehow the short game keeps sneaking out of the alley with the only clean shoes in the bag. That can work for a stretch, but it’s the kind of profile that leaves you staring at the screen wondering how a guy can be both irritatingly survivable and still one bad hole away from a mutiny. The recipe is messy, but not dead. If the big stick ever stops starting fights, there’s a golfer in here.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: DRIVER CASTING SHADOWS, WEDGES DOING COMMUNITY SERVICE
profiles.profile: This one lives in the land of almost. The long game has enough juice to tease you, but the scoring picture keeps getting kneecapped by weak short-game output and just enough putting nonsense to stop anything from getting properly hot. There’s some sneaky recovery talent buried in the card, which is why the whole thing doesn’t faceplant every time out, but the overall vibe is still very much ‘good luck piecing together 18 holes without at least one catastrophe.’ Solid chaos. Not clean chaos, but chaos.

profiles.name: derekldavis
profiles.tagline: SURVIVAL GOLF WITH A BROKEN MIDDLE GEARSHAFT
profiles.profile: One start, one very expensive reminder that the middle of the bag was not invited. The putter at least didn’t completely betray the effort, but the rest of it was a head-to-toe shank parade with the driver, irons, and wedges all taking turns setting the clubhouse on fire. The weird part is the card found a few birdies in the rubble, which means there’s some pulse here; it’s just buried under a pile of tee-to-green punishment. Extremely rough debut, but not a total empty room.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GAME IN NEED OF A WARRANT
profiles.profile: The signature here is pretty clear: if the approach play doesn’t cooperate, everything else gets dragged behind the truck. The driver hasn’t exactly been handing out free looks either, so the whole setup tends to start behind the eight-ball and stay there. There are flashes of short-game rescue work, but they’ve mostly been asked to cover for a lot of trench warfare from tee to green. This is a card that can survive a while on grit, then promptly trip over its own ball-striking and spill the drink.
